newsitem.title: DENMARK: B&O set for continuing growth in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: B&O set for continuing growth in 1997/98.

text.p: Upmarket Danish audio/video and television maker Bang & Olufsen (B&0) on Wednesday posted full year 1996/97 pre-tax profits 11 percent up on the previous year and forecast 15 percent growth in earnings in 1997/98.

"The result is as expected and exceeds our growth targets. The audio/video market in most European countries is still flat, so our result must be considered very satisfactory in that light," B&O said in a statement.

B&O reported pre-tax profits for full year 1996/97 of 321 million crowns ($45.2 million), compared to 1995/96's interim 272 million crowns and slightly lower than market analysts' expectations of an average 333 million crowns.

Two years ago B&O set annual targets of five percent growth in annual turnover, 15 percent in earnings and 10 percent in profits and these goals had been met in 1996/97 and would be again in 1997/98, it said.

It said its audio/video sales achieved solid growth in virtually all markets, at between 10 percent and 32 percent in Italy, Switzerland, United States, Netherlands, Belgium, Japan and Russia, aided by better agent and distribution networks.
In B&O's two biggest audio markets, Denmark and Germany, the growth rate was only four percent and five percent in Britain, B&O said.

It said its B&O Telecom unit, which produces mobile and cordless telephones, reported improved profits and turnover, while B&O Technology, which makes medical products, noted increased profits on unchanged sales.

B&O said its buyback of Dutch electronic giant Philips' 25 percent stake in the company, announced last May, would mean a 297 million crown reduction in financial income for 1997/97. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
